inventions for circumventing obstacles, i.e.

  • use water droplets of ultrapure water disperse light so that sharp edges can be made with more powerful supercomputers

  • pinch wafers while spraying rigid layers of them, because a stretched layer is a better layer

Plus, evolution of computers is done in baby steps, at a micro level, if you will. Once peek efficiency is reached, then developers start to look for small leaps in design that can allow for a higher peek.

For example, in the 70's, circuit boards were two sided. Designs only allowed for so much efficiency until the board could no longer get smaller. Then the idea of multilayered breadboards came out and it allowed for more chips and more circuit paths to be layed out while maintaining the same size board. Which then allowed for more efficiency circuit laying. Then, by the 90's, motherboards consisted of 5 layers and 50x the chips while still the same dimension.

Evolution can't be had until the next leap is made.
